input: Under COLREGs Rule 5, every vessel shall at all times maintain a proper look-out by which of the following?
choices: Radar observation, but only when visibility is restricted
Sight and hearing as well as all available means appropriate in the prevailing circumstances
Sight alone, with radar and AIS as optional supplements
Continuous AIS and radar monitoring, which together satisfy the look-out requirement

input: Under COLREGs Rule 7, if there is any doubt as to whether risk of collision exists with an approaching vessel, what shall be assumed?
choices: Risk does not exist until confirmed by radar plotting
Risk exists only if the other vessel is within 3 nautical miles
Such risk shall be deemed to exist
The give-way vessel will resolve the doubt by manoeuvring first

input: Two power-driven vessels are meeting on reciprocal courses so as to involve risk of collision (a head-on situation). Under COLREGs Rule 14, what action is required?
choices: Each vessel shall alter her course to starboard so that each passes on the port side of the other
The faster vessel shall alter course while the slower vessel stands on
Each vessel shall alter her course to port so that each passes on the starboard side of the other
Both vessels shall stop engines and communicate by VHF before manoeuvring

input: Two power-driven vessels are crossing so as to involve risk of collision. Under COLREGs Rule 15, which vessel shall keep out of the way?
choices: The vessel which is to windward of the other
The vessel which has the other on her own port side
The smaller of the two vessels
The vessel which has the other on her own starboard side

input: Under UNCLOS Article 17, which ships enjoy the right of innocent passage through the territorial sea?
choices: Ships of all States, whether coastal or land-locked
Only ships of States that share a maritime boundary with the coastal State
Only merchant ships, with government ships excluded
Only ships that have obtained prior authorisation from the coastal State

input: Under UNCLOS Article 18, passage through the territorial sea must be continuous and expeditious. In which of the following circumstances may a ship nevertheless stop and anchor?
choices: Whenever the master considers it commercially convenient
When stopping is incidental to ordinary navigation, or rendered necessary by force majeure or distress, or to render assistance to persons, ships or aircraft in danger
Only after receiving express clearance from the coastal State's port authority
Whenever the ship remains more than 3 nautical miles from the coast

input: Under UNCLOS Article 20, how are submarines required to navigate when exercising innocent passage in the territorial sea?
choices: Submerged, provided they proceed at a safe speed
At periscope depth, provided they broadcast their position on AIS
On the surface, but only inside designated sea lanes
On the surface and showing their flag

input: Which State bears the primary responsibility for ensuring that a merchant ship on the high seas complies with international safety, manning and pollution standards?
choices: The State in whose waters the ship was last inspected
The State of the ship's beneficial owner
The flag State whose flag the ship is entitled to fly
The nearest coastal State at the time of the voyage

input: A foreign-flagged cargo ship is voluntarily in port when inspectors find deficiencies that are clearly hazardous to safety. Under port State control, what may the port State do?
choices: Nothing beyond reporting the deficiencies to the flag State
Inspect the ship and detain her until the deficiencies that are clearly hazardous are rectified
Prosecute the crew under the flag State's national law
Revoke the ship's registration and certificates

input: In which maritime zone does the coastal State exercise full sovereignty, subject to the right of innocent passage for foreign ships?
choices: The exclusive economic zone
The contiguous zone
The high seas
The territorial sea

input: Under COLREGs Rule 5, what is the stated purpose of maintaining a proper look-out?
choices: To make a full appraisal of the situation and of the risk of collision
To comply with the vessel's safety management system records
To detect navigational marks for position fixing
To maintain a continuous listening watch on VHF channel 16

input: Under COLREGs Rule 6, every vessel shall at all times proceed at a safe speed. What must that speed allow the vessel to do?
choices: Maintain her berth arrival time within charter-party tolerances
Take proper and effective action to avoid collision and be stopped within a distance appropriate to the prevailing circumstances and conditions
Keep pace with surrounding traffic so as not to impede the flow
Reach the next waypoint without altering her engine setting

input: A vessel is navigating in clear weather with her radar switched on and operational. Under COLREGs Rule 6, are radar-related factors relevant to her choice of safe speed?
choices: No — radar factors apply only in restricted visibility
No — Rule 6 concerns engine capability, not sensors
Yes — vessels with operational radar must additionally account for factors such as the radar's characteristics, efficiency and limitations
Only if the vessel is over 10,000 gross tonnes

input: Under COLREGs Rule 7, which of the following is an acceptable basis for determining whether risk of collision exists?
choices: Assumptions made on the basis of scanty radar information
The other vessel's AIS destination field
Visual impressions alone, since electronic aids may mislead
Careful watching of the compass bearing of an approaching vessel, with risk deemed to exist if the bearing does not appreciably change

input: Under COLREGs Rule 7, can risk of collision sometimes exist even when an appreciable bearing change is evident?
choices: Yes — particularly when approaching a very large vessel or a tow, or when approaching a vessel at close range
No — an appreciable bearing change always means the vessels will pass clear
Only when both vessels are power-driven
Only inside a traffic separation scheme

input: Under COLREGs Rule 8, any alteration of course and/or speed to avoid collision shall, if the circumstances of the case admit, be:
choices: Executed as a series of small adjustments so the track change is gradual
Withheld until the vessels are within VHF range to coordinate
Large enough to be readily apparent to another vessel observing visually or by radar
Limited to speed changes, since course changes confuse radar observers

input: Under COLREGs Rule 8, if necessary to avoid collision or allow more time to assess the situation, a vessel shall:
choices: Sound at least five short and rapid blasts
Slacken her speed or take all way off by stopping or reversing her means of propulsion
Alter course to port and increase speed
Hold course and speed until the other vessel acts

input: Under COLREGs Rule 14, when a vessel is in any doubt as to whether a head-on situation exists, what shall she do?
choices: Treat the situation as a crossing and stand on
Stop engines and await clarification by VHF
Sound one prolonged blast and maintain course
Assume that the head-on situation exists and act accordingly

input: Under COLREGs Rule 15, the give-way vessel in a crossing situation shall, if the circumstances of the case admit, avoid doing what?
choices: Crossing ahead of the other vessel
Reducing speed below steerage way
Altering course by more than 30 degrees
Passing astern of the other vessel

input: Under COLREGs Rule 17, what is the stand-on vessel initially required to do when another vessel is obliged to keep out of her way?
choices: Alter course to starboard to make her intentions clear
Reduce speed as a precaution while holding course
Keep her course and speed
Engage hand steering and post additional look-outs

input: Under COLREGs Rule 17, when the stand-on vessel finds herself so close that collision cannot be avoided by the action of the give-way vessel alone, what shall she do?
choices: Continue to hold course and speed, as Rule 17 forbids her to manoeuvre
Take such action as will best aid to avoid collision
Alter course to port toward the give-way vessel's stern in all cases
Sound the danger signal and wait for the give-way vessel to respond

input: Under UNCLOS Article 19, passage of a foreign ship is innocent so long as it is not prejudicial to which interests of the coastal State?
choices: Its fiscal revenues and customs tariffs only
Its commercial shipping interests
Its fishing industry's market share
The peace, good order or security of the coastal State

input: Under UNCLOS Article 19(2), which of the following activities by a foreign ship in the territorial sea is considered prejudicial to the peace, good order or security of the coastal State?
choices: Navigating with engines at full sea speed
Any fishing activities
Stopping to render assistance to persons in danger
Using an automatic identification system transponder

input: Under UNCLOS Article 19(2), carrying out research or survey activities during passage through the territorial sea has what effect?
choices: It renders the passage non-innocent
It is permitted if the data is shared with the coastal State
It is permitted for hydrographic but not military survey
It has no effect on the character of the passage

input: Under UNCLOS Article 21, foreign ships exercising the right of innocent passage shall comply with which of the following?
choices: Only the laws of their flag State
The coastal State's laws and regulations relating to innocent passage and all generally accepted international regulations relating to the prevention of collisions at sea
Coastal State laws only when escorted by a coastal State vessel
IMO circulars, but not coastal State legislation

input: Under UNCLOS Article 22, what may a coastal State require of foreign ships exercising innocent passage where necessary for the safety of navigation?
choices: That they embark a coastal State pilot in all cases
That they transit only in daylight hours
That they use such sea lanes and traffic separation schemes as the coastal State may designate or prescribe
That they post a transit bond with the port authority

input: Under UNCLOS Article 24, which of the following describes the coastal State's basic duty regarding innocent passage?
choices: It may hamper passage whenever national interest requires
It shall not hamper the innocent passage of foreign ships except in accordance with the Convention
It must escort all foreign ships through the territorial sea
It must provide free pilotage and towage services

input: Under UNCLOS Article 25, a coastal State may temporarily suspend innocent passage of foreign ships in specified areas of its territorial sea under which conditions?
choices: Without conditions, at any time, for any class of ships
If the suspension is essential for the protection of its security, applies without discrimination among foreign ships, and takes effect only after being duly published
Only with the prior consent of all flag States concerned
Only during armed conflict formally declared by the coastal State

input: Under UNCLOS Article 94, the flag State must effectively exercise its jurisdiction and control over ships flying its flag in which matters?
choices: Administrative, technical and social matters
Cargo insurance and freight rates
Crew nationality quotas
Port tariffs charged to the ship

input: What is the primary purpose of a port State control inspection of a foreign-flagged ship?
choices: To re-measure the ship's gross tonnage for harbour dues
To audit the commercial terms of the ship's charter
To verify that the condition of the ship and its equipment comply with the requirements of international conventions and that it is manned and operated in compliance with them
To assess the ship for entry into the port State's national registry

metadata.rule: Port State control (SOLAS Ch. I Reg. 19; MARPOL Art. 5)

input: On the high seas, which State's jurisdiction does a merchant ship fall under as a general rule?
choices: The State of the nearest coastline at any given moment
The exclusive jurisdiction of its flag State, save in exceptional cases provided for in international law
Concurrent jurisdiction of all States whose nationals are aboard
The jurisdiction of the State where the voyage began

input: Which entity issues (or authorises recognised organisations to issue) a ship's international safety certificates?
choices: The port State of the ship's next call
The IMO Secretariat directly
The shipowner's protection and indemnity club
The ship's flag State administration

metadata.rule: Flag-state certification (SOLAS Ch. I; UNCLOS Article 94)

input: How does the legal regime of internal waters (e.g., inside a port) differ from that of the territorial sea?
choices: There is no difference; both are subject to innocent passage
Internal waters fall under full coastal State sovereignty and foreign ships have no general right of innocent passage there, unlike in the territorial sea
Internal waters are governed by the flag State of the visiting ship
Coastal State law applies in internal waters only with flag State consent

input: A coastal State suspects a foreign merchant ship of infringing its customs laws within its contiguous zone. What control may the coastal State exercise there under UNCLOS?
choices: The control necessary to prevent and punish infringement of its customs, fiscal, immigration or sanitary laws within its territory or territorial sea
Full sovereignty identical to internal waters
None; the contiguous zone confers no enforcement competence
Only the right to demand the ship lower its flag

input: Under UNCLOS Article 30, if a warship does not comply with the coastal State's laws concerning passage through the territorial sea and disregards a request for compliance, what may the coastal State do?
choices: Board and arrest the warship's commanding officer
Confiscate the warship as security for damages
Require the warship to leave the territorial sea immediately
Refer the warship's officers to its national criminal courts
